short: The final wartime meeting of the Big Three finalized the occupation of Germany and issued an ultimatum to Japan.
full:
Between 17 July and 2 August 1945, Allied leaders met at Potsdam, near Berlin, to finalize agreements reached at Yalta. The personnel had changed: US President Harry S. Truman replaced the deceased Roosevelt, and Clement Attlee replaced Churchill midway through the conference after winning the British general election. Stalin remained for the Soviet Union. The leaders confirmed the division of Germany, agreed on the prosecution of Nazi war criminals, and shifted Germany's eastern border to the Oder-Neisse line.

During the conference, Truman was informed of the successful Trinity atomic bomb test. On 26 July, the United States, Britain, and China issued the Potsdam Declaration, demanding the unconditional surrender of Japan or facing prompt and utter destruction. Japan's initial rejection of the ultimatum led directly to the atomic bombings.
